columns.name: invoice_id
columns.description: Invoice number, kept as text. A leading C marks a cancellation invoice; see is_cancellation.
columns.rationale: Profile shows null_rate 0.0 and distinct_count 2330 over 44,721 rows, consistent with the committed required text identifier.

columns.name: is_cancellation
columns.description: True when invoice_id carries the C cancellation prefix. Cancellations are retained and flagged, not dropped, so conservation arithmetic against bronze stays auditable.
columns.rationale: Profile shows null_rate 0.0 and distinct_count 2 (false, true), matching the committed boolean required column.

columns.name: stock_code
columns.description: Product code as landed, kept as text; alphanumeric suffixes and non-product adjustment codes occur.
columns.rationale: Profile shows null_rate 0.0 and distinct_count 3141, matching the committed required text identifier.

columns.name: product_description
columns.description: Product description, whitespace-trimmed; nulls are retained rather than imputed.
columns.rationale: Profile measures null_rate 0.005098 (228 nulls of 44,721 rows), a nonzero rate that keeps this column optional as committed.

columns.name: quantity
columns.description: Units on the line. Negative values occur both on cancellation-invoice lines and on zero-unit-price stock-adjustment lines; consumers must not infer cancellation from negative quantity alone.
columns.rationale: Profile shows null_rate 0.0, min -1395, max 5184, matching the committed required integer column.

columns.name: invoiced_at
columns.description: Invoice timestamp, strictly cast from the landed text representation. On within-invoice clock-drift duplicates the earliest scan tick wins.
columns.rationale: Profile shows null_rate 0.0 with min 2009-12-01T07:45:00 and max 2009-12-23T16:58:00, matching the committed required timestamp column.

columns.name: unit_price
columns.description: Unit price in sterling. Zero-price lines (freebies and adjustments) are retained; negative prices are contract-invalid.
columns.rationale: Profile shows null_rate 0.0, min 0.0, max 1998.49, matching the committed required decimal column and its non-negative rule.

columns.name: customer_id
columns.description: Customer identifier. The bronze null rate is retained as null (guest or unregistered checkouts), not dropped and not imputed.
columns.rationale: Profile measures null_rate 0.300664 (13,446 nulls of 44,721 rows), a substantial nonzero rate that keeps this column optional as committed.

columns.name: country
columns.rationale: Profile shows null_rate 0.0 and distinct_count 24, matching the committed required text column.

columns.name: captured_at
columns.description: Capture timestamp carried forward from the bronze landing (_airbyte_extracted_at), marking when the surviving line's earliest capture entered the pipeline. This is the incremental watermark the gold layer relies on; it is required because every surviving line now carries a populated captured_at value, so consumers can treat it as always present for watermarking and incremental processing.
columns.rationale: Fresh profile measures null_rate 0.0 for captured_at over 44,721 rows, confirming the incremental path has landed and the column is now always populated.

purpose: The cleaned, typed, one-row-per-invoice-line view of the Online Retail II sample: the first contracted silver table and the sole silver input to the gold unified event star.
usage: Read silver.silver_invoice_lines for line-level retail sales analysis. Cancellation lines are retained and flagged (is_cancellation); consumers aggregating revenue must filter or net them deliberately. Zero-price lines are retained.
limitations: Exact duplicate bronze rows are treated as capture artifacts and excluded, so identical legitimate re-scans are indistinguishable and also excluded; the residual grain is the distinct line. Rows identical in every business column except invoicedate are collapsed to one line with the earliest timestamp retained. customer_id is null for guest or unregistered checkouts and those rows are retained with customer_id null.
